title: Net art, immersive tech, and The Couple in the Cage
introduction: This week the session moved into net art and immersive technologies, and set out how we are going to study them properly: reading the literature, working through the tutorials, and keeping pace so the material does not run away from us. I also watched The Couple in the Cage, Coco Fusco and Paula Heredia's 1993 video, which has been turning over in my mind as my group and I try to settle the concept for our project.
related_work: The course plan for net art and immersive technologies is clear: we go deep rather than broad, and that means investing real time in the readings and the tutorials. The emphasis on reading documents is the part I want to hold on to, because it is the difference between describing these art forms and understanding them critically. The Couple in the Cage is a thirty-minute single-channel video directed by Coco Fusco and Paula Heredia. It documents a 1992 performance in which Fusco and Guillermo Gómez-Peña toured the US, Spain, England and Australia posing as 'undiscovered Amerindians' from Guatinaui, a fictional island supposedly missed by Columbus. Sitting in a gilded cage in plazas, museums and shopping malls, they performed made-up 'traditional tasks' — lifting weights, watching television, writing on a laptop — while the video intercuts their performances with archival footage of real indigenous people displayed in circuses and sideshows.
method: I watched the video once straight through to feel it, then went back to note how it is built: the way it cuts between the staged cage and the archival images, and the way it keeps returning to the faces of the spectators. Around it, I have been reading the assigned material on net art and immersive technologies, and talking with my group about what our project should actually be about.
results_discussion: What struck me most about The Couple in the Cage is how many of the spectators believed the couple were genuine captives, even phoning the Humane Society to complain. The work is a satirical reenactment of the human zoos and sideshows that really did display indigenous people, but what it reveals is not just that history — it reveals how ready we are to accept a performance as real when the frame looks authoritative. That idea of the frame, the museum label, the cage, the official tone, feels very close to what I want to do. It has definitely given me something for our project, though we are still discussing the concept itself, and I have not yet settled what we are actually trying to say.
conclusion_future_work: My takeaway is that the reading and the tutorials are not homework to get through, they are how I build a critical hold on net art and immersive technologies, so I am going to keep pace rather than catch up later. The Couple in the Cage has given me a question to carry into the group discussion: how much of what an audience believes is shaped by the frame around it, rather than by the content itself. Once we settle our project's concept, I want to bring that question to the making.
references: Fusco, C. and Heredia, P. (1993) The Couple in the Cage: A Guatinaui Odyssey [Video]. Available at: https://www.moma.org/collection/works/403501 (Accessed: 27 October 2026).
